topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and introduces the multi-perspective scope of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Cellular Differentiation and Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer biologically as a progressive breakdown of developmental differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor Progression, Invasion, and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how tumors progress from contained, benign lesions into invasive and metastatic malignancies across clinical and histological contexts.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standard naming rules, suffixes, and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms across tissue lineages.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Causes of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the mechanical, metabolic, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Humans and Other Species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare the frequency, common anatomical sites, and mortality patterns of tumors across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the rationale, practical methods, and variable effectiveness of population screening programs for early cancer detection across different organs.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing administrative framing, referencing the learning outcomes and looking ahead to the practical sessions.
